sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Perry County
sections.html:
A Perry County deed can be filed in only one place, Hazard. The recording department of the County Clerk is at 481 Main Street, Suite 102. Call 606-439-0557 for recording, which keeps Monday-to-Friday hours from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon. The main clerk line is 606-436-4614. Call before you drive in to confirm the day's hours.

Walking in is only one option. Four e-recording services are named on the clerk's land records page (Indecomm, CSC, Simplifile and ePN), and eCCLIX, the clerk's subscription index, lets attorneys, title agents and lenders read recorded instruments remotely. The index reaches back to 1993 and document images to 2000, so older instruments may call for a written request with a book and page.

sections.h2: What a deed must show before the clerk accepts it
sections.html:
Every deed is screened by clerk's staff before it is filed, and one missing element sends it back. Make sure yours has:

  • Names and mailing addresses for grantor and grantee, a legal description, and the source of title.
  • A preparation statement and a return address for the recorded original.
  • A mailing address for the next tax bill (KRS 382.135).
  • A sworn consideration statement signed by both parties before a notary, and the grantor's own notarized signature.

Gift deeds give an estimated fair cash value in place of a price. Utility-easement deeds and deeds correcting an earlier one between the same parties need no consideration statement. When a house passes by will or intestacy, the personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk before the estate closes. Quit claim deeds convey only the grantor's interest and carry no warranty of title.

sections.h2: Records research: what the index covers
sections.html:
If you need an older deed, start with what the clerk's tools can reach. eCCLIX, the subscription index, goes back to 1993, and images of documents go back to 2000. Anything before those years may require a written request that includes the book and page. Attorneys, title agents and lenders usually subscribe, so a seller with a closing agent seldom needs to do this alone.

When you write for a copy, give the clerk a book and page, an instrument number, or details such as the borrower, the lender and the loan amount. Without one of those, staff cannot find the paper because they are not allowed to search titles. If you cannot locate a recorded deed, an attorney, paralegal or abstractor can do the search. The clerk's office keeps a list of people who produce insured title work.

The clerk's schedule lists minimums by document type, and these entries come up most in a sale or an estate.

Minimum recording fees on the Perry County Clerk's schedule

Deed$50
Deed of correction$46
Easement$50
Mortgage$80
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46
Power of attorney$50
Affidavit of descent$50
Will$47
Certificate of delinquency release$46

Each page after the fifth adds $3 on most entries; mortgages add $3 only after page 30. Because these are minimums, a long document costs more, and a closing agent will usually total the recording charges for the settlement statement.

sections.h2: How transfer tax works on a sale
sections.html:
Sellers pay this one. KRS 142.050 sets 50 cents on every $500 block of the price in the deed, with a partial block counted as a full one. The clerk collects before recording, retains 5% for handling it, and remits the rest to the county treasurer each quarter.

  • Exempt: transfers between spouses or ex-spouses in a divorce, foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu, partitions, and tax-sale deeds.
  • Exempt: parent-to-child and grandparent-to-grandchild transfers made for nominal consideration.
  • Gifts and nominal-price deeds are measured at estimated market value instead.

A clerk who records a taxable deed without collecting can be fined $50 per offense.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and liens at the clerk's office
sections.html:
Once April 15 closes the sheriff's year, unpaid bills arrive at the clerk as certificates of delinquency and are recorded as liens on the parcels. Interest accrues monthly, commissions are added, and the county attorney sends written notice. Revenue sets the clerk's sale at no sooner than ninety days and no later than 135 days after the handover.

The clerk's site points owners to a delinquent tax application, and eligible owners may arrange a payment plan with the county attorney. If an outside purchaser buys a certificate, the fee schedule shows $30 to record the assignment and $46 to record the release afterward. A seller carrying an open certificate should pay it, have the release recorded, and give the title company proof before closing.

sections.h2: Can clerk staff run a title search?
sections.html:
No. Staff are barred from searching titles, though they will help a visitor browse the books. Copy requests must be written and must carry a book and page, an instrument number, or enough particulars (borrower, lender, loan amount) to locate the paper without a search. The office keeps names of attorneys, paralegals and abstractors who produce insured title work.

The clerk's site also advertises DocAlert, a free notice service. It emails an owner whenever a deed or mortgage is filed under that name, an early warning for owners of empty or estate houses.

Perry County has 26,555 residents for 2025, down from 28,473 in the 2020 count. Hazard is the seat, and Buckhorn is the other city. Households number 11,481, and 70.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The median value of an owned home is $91,800, gross rent is $798, and owner costs run $1,167 with a mortgage. Household income is $42,181 at the midpoint. Of the 13,213 housing units counted in 2020, 13.1 percent stood vacant, which points to a lot of empty property.

Many addresses sit in named hollows and creek communities such as Ary, Bulan, Busy, Chavies, Dwarf, Happy, Typo and Viper, so ask the clerk how a parcel is indexed before searching by street address. Landlords and sole proprietors selling a rental or a business property should also know that the county charges a 1% occupational license tax on wages and net profit, and that anyone working inside Hazard city limits owes the county and the city.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell in Perry County
sections.html:
A little preparation avoids delays. Decide whether your closing agent will record on paper or electronically, since the e-recording services listed above skip the drive to Hazard. Ask for one total covering recording fees and transfer tax. Confirm the legal description and the source of title, since the clerk rejects a deed that omits either. If the house is vacant or part of an estate, consider signing up for DocAlert so you hear about any filing made under your name.

Finally, check for open certificates before you list. A written payoff and a recorded release are far easier to arrange before a buyer is waiting, and the title company will want to see both.

faqs.q: What is the address for recording a deed in Perry County?
faqs.a: 481 Main Street, Suite 102, Hazard, KY 41701. Recording is open weekdays from eight to four.

faqs.q: What is the clerk's fee for a Perry County deed?
faqs.a: Fifty dollars is the posted minimum, with $3 added per page beyond five. Transfer tax on the deed's stated value is a separate charge.

faqs.q: Can closing documents be recorded electronically in Perry County?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk's land records page names Indecomm, CSC, Simplifile and ePN as e-recording services.

faqs.q: Which party owes transfer tax on a Perry County deed?
faqs.a: The seller does, as grantor, at 50 cents for each $500 block of the price, with a partial block counted as full.

faqs.q: Will the Perry County Clerk look up my parcel's title?
faqs.a: No, staff cannot perform a title search. They can help you browse, and written copy requests need a book and page, instrument number or similar detail.
